turns.content: For S(n,k)=a_{n-1}+...+a_{n-k}, define m_n and M_n as the minimum and maximum of S(n,k)/k over 1<=k<=n, and let Delta_n=M_n-m_n. Explain why a_{2018}-a_{2017}<=Delta_{2018}.
Prove that for n>2, Delta_n<=(n-1)Delta_{n-1}/n by comparing the extremal averages at stage n with a_{n-1} and the stage-(n-1) interval.
In that case, what upper bound follows for a_{2018}-a_{2017}?
Show that no term exceeds 1, then define q as the first index with a_q<1 and determine a_q.
Compute Delta_{q+1}, then iterate the contraction inequality through Delta_{2018} and simplify the resulting telescoping product.
Use q<=2017 to obtain a universal upper bound for a_{2018}-a_{2017}, and combine it with the all-ones case.
Construct an admissible sequence attaining that bound: take a_1=...=a_{2016}=1 and choose the required averages for a_{2017} and a_{2018}. Verify both terms.
Conclude the maximal possible value of a_{2018}-a_{2017}.
Because every new term is an average of preceding terms, determine whether it can ever lie outside the preceding global minimum-to-maximum range.
Check that the extremal construction and the range property are mutually consistent, including the strict drop at index 2017 and the following rise.
Report the sharp maximum and the admissible-term range property.
